headline: Stricter benchmarks expose failure modes in structure-based binder and ligand design
label: Structure Informed Binder Evaluation
summary: Docking, binder design, and interface prediction are being re-evaluated under held-out, budgeted, and diagnostic protocols.
synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluation of structure-informed ligand and interface prediction under stricter conditions. PMO-Dock benchmarks docking-based molecular optimization across 25 tasks with a specificity task, held-out tests, and strict oracle budgets. A BindCraft2 analysis attributes zero binders from 627 cyclic-peptide trajectories against LDHA K81 to a pLDDT screen gate and a loss mismatch. Prospective work couples fragment-based generative design with alchemical absolute binding free-energy ranking to prioritize LasB inhibitors, and an aptamer study runs LLM-agent closed-loop iteration against wet-lab bead-binding data. Other items address LLM inference of partner-dependent mutation effects and enzyme expression, so the thread is dominant rather than universal. What is new is the explicit diagnosis of design-pipeline failure modes alongside experimentally validated ranking of generated candidates.
